purpose: Retain portable observations and tensions independently of a chosen chapter. A reported preference does not establish a tested gem or adoption.

ideas.title: Less time inside the same distance
ideas.idea: A fixed spatial path becomes a different encounter when its pace changes.
ideas.anchor: The rods have not grown, but there is less time inside the same distance.
ideas.evidence: Supplied packet reading identifies this sentence as worth preserving. Code shares X positions at four rates; no headset sensation is inferred.
ideas.risk: Conflating speed with another source of randomness or prescribing a feeling.
ideas.next_test: Compare which draft makes the pace change matter without explaining an emotion.

ideas.title: Marks become available after withdrawal
ideas.idea: Movement leaves a surface that can be examined when following has ended.
ideas.evidence: The supplied reading asks for more attention to the recording wall. Current ink persists after release; return motion adds no marks.
ideas.risk: Treating the image as a complete recording of the bodily event.
ideas.next_test: Does the reader want to compare marks, revisit a motion, or inspect a dark patch?

later_studies.relation: Close observation makes the distinction between destinations and travel the work's central discovery.

ideas.title: A dense image does not identify its source
ideas.idea: Selected destinations and interpolated travel both contribute to the visible marks.
ideas.evidence: Installed targets are uniform; twelve phase samples per segment contribute ink. Gaussian generation exists in reconstruction code without a room selector.
ideas.risk: Inferring a Gaussian source from a crowded centre, or offering a control absent from the exhibit.
ideas.next_test: Retain endpoints and path samples separately in a future reconstruction; compare their distributions.

later_candidates.detail: That is a fact about our selection, not evidence that the group deserved it.
later_candidates.assessment: The amber selection extends reading time and visibility without establishing significance; editorial attention, not an independent reader result.

ideas.title: Production, recording and selection
ideas.idea: A hand can change which result stays available without having produced that result.
ideas.evidence: Earlier user response distinguishes producing, recording and selecting. Touch toggles a generated five-digit group; release of the hand alone does not release it.
ideas.risk: Flattening all kinds of keeping into one metaphor, or implying a complete table proves provenance.
ideas.next_test: Can a reader distinguish what the touch changes here from what it changes at the abacus?

later_studies.relation: One integer organizes an investigation into what a dated receipt can establish.
Montage keeps the acquisition date beside calculated playback without a continuous explanation.

ideas.title: A date interrupts a repeating present
ideas.idea: A retained acquisition document and a replaying calculation have different temporalities.
ideas.evidence: Supplied reading values the receipt beside the repeating gaps. The receipt reports 435 acquired on 13 October; the current sequence is synthesized and reused.
ideas.risk: Making the receipt prove more than it records, or treating later clicks as new physical measurements.
ideas.next_test: Does documentary interruption create curiosity without requiring a second explanatory summary?

ideas.title: A clock loses a distinction while the sound keeps it
ideas.idea: The same retained event times can yield different measured comparisons.
ideas.evidence: Changing comparison resolution preserves events/audio; equal measured intervals are skipped.
ideas.risk: Confusing quantization with changed event timing or asserting every coarser comparison loses the same amount.
ideas.next_test: Keep the same trace, change resolution, and ask what disappeared from which representation.

later_candidates.detail: At the rods, a sequence of numbers gave the hand a journey. Here a journey gives the other instruments a number.
later_candidates.assessment: The reversal relates the sampler to the opening. Placement remains conditional; no new gesture or collision pair has been demonstrated.

later_studies.relation: The absent station is acknowledged as an absence; no gesture is invented to complete the itinerary.

ideas.title: A movement becomes one of a thousand beginnings
ideas.idea: Bodily input can alter a generator while many distinctions in its measurement do not survive the seed mapping.
ideas.evidence: Pose records are rounded, hashed and reduced modulo 1000. Different records can collide; no found pair is claimed. The saved room currently removes this part.
ideas.risk: Describing an absent stop as installed, certifying true randomness, or claiming an unperformed collision trial.
ideas.next_test: Resolve placement; retain two different records with the same seed and compare consequences.

later_studies.relation: Performance separates the sphere's continuing cycle from the person's renewed approach.
A fictional request creates conflict between selecting a seed and changing the return rule.

ideas.title: Another draw cannot repeal the return
ideas.idea: Variation within an excursion and alteration of its route rule are different capacities.
ideas.evidence: User's full reading found the distinction consequential. Direction/distance vary while the sphere's return remains authored; release ends body carry.
ideas.risk: Equating the sphere's compulsory return with a player being forced to remain attached.
ideas.next_test: Does the ending prompt another seed choice or a proposal to alter the rule—and why?
ideas.latest_test: 2026-10-16: actual-hall synthetic desktop release disconnects carrying while the sphere continues and returns; 28-check receipt in book-as-recorder. Reader preference for the event-led ending remains open.

ideas.title: A visible cell can cease to support a body
ideas.idea: A computational distinction can arrive as a spatial event before it receives an explanation.
ideas.anchor: The faint tile can still be seen after it can no longer carry you.
ideas.evidence: Supplied packet reading prefers this CA encounter. It belongs to CA_ExpandingSpace, not Random Definition; proximity affects health and support thresholds.
ideas.risk: Importing a bridge into the wrong room, prescribing a moral, or describing pressure sensing.
ideas.next_test: Look for a comparably precise consequence in randomness without copying the bridge's plot.

ideas.title: Replay supplies events, not the first encounter
ideas.idea: The procedure can repeat while recognition, attention and reading duration change.
ideas.evidence: Repeatable paths and event lists are implemented. What a listener or visitor learns from repetition remains open.
ideas.risk: Claiming an inevitable response to repetition or treating reading speed as simulated time.
ideas.next_test: Ask what changed on the second reading or hearing; retain a report of no gain.

ideas.title: A new record would keep the release point
ideas.idea: An encounter can reveal something the apparatus does not currently preserve.
ideas.evidence: Candidate A imagines wanting a mark where carry ends. No such mark is asserted to exist.
ideas.risk: Making a narrator's proposal look like a participant request or a shipped feature.
ideas.next_test: Does another reader want this record; what would it let them compare?

later_candidates.detail: The paper does not record the hurry.
later_candidates.assessment: A concise spatial/temporal distinction under equal completed segments and unchanged sampling. The image omits this duration; the full system need not lose it.

ideas.title: Accumulation loses arrival order
ideas.idea: A static surface can preserve where marks accumulated while failing to preserve the order of the events that made them.
ideas.evidence: Study 4 asks what can be recovered from darkness. The current wall uses identical translucent circles sampled by segment phase, without arrival-order encoding. Equal completed segments can produce the same mark locations at different speeds; equal elapsed time is not the same comparison.
ideas.risk: Claiming the complete system loses its sequence, rather than specifying the information absent from this image; treating a proposed comparison as an observed visit.
ideas.next_test: Compare images after equal completed segments at two rates. Keep the ordered event records separately and ask which distinctions the images alone can support.

ideas.title: A beginning is not a complete cause
ideas.idea: A seed can be retained exactly while the procedures that give it consequences remain unspecified by that record.
ideas.evidence: Study 2 corrects cause to starting input. The receipt records acquisition of 435; instruments retain separate generators, requests and mappings. The receipt does not document all those procedures or authenticate the later simulated clicks.
ideas.risk: Implying a seed has no causal role, that all instruments share one advancing stream, or that no adequate reconstruction record is possible.
ideas.next_test: Hold 435 fixed and change one documented mapping or generator procedure. Retain enough configuration and state to reconstruct both results; distinguish that record from the seed alone.

ideas.title: The book is another recorder
ideas.idea: Moving between hall, prose, image and numerical table changes which differences survive. A reduction can expose a relationship while losing another.
ideas.evidence: The supplied critique identifies selection across media. The new edition preserves wall-image hashes, distinguishes a rule diagram from captured evidence, and places an actual RGB grouping beside digit groups. Its literary effect remains untested. The supplied Recorder Edition reading finds this relationship stronger. A follow-up now pairs unchanged arrival captures with scripted native consequences; literary effectiveness remains open.
ideas.risk: Making the book explain its own meaning repeatedly, or filling missing captured evidence with invented marks.
ideas.next_test: Read with and without the release schematic; name what becomes available and what imagination it forecloses.

ideas.title: A baseline needs a consequence
ideas.idea: A picture of an apparatus and a picture after an intervention can expose what the apparatus retains without making either picture stand in for lived experience.
ideas.evidence: 32 native checks pass; reconstructed abacus and page baselines match archived pixels exactly. After 48 segments each row keeps 576 marks; after two rows the selected 33442 stays while its neighbour advances.
ideas.risk: Tiny numerals can hide the difference. Outline conversion discards density and amber; a still cannot show speed. Scripted contact is not a human trial.
ideas.next_test: Deferred: compare abacus recording treatments when the author returns to this study. The RAND pair is retired; contour remains the current book choice.
ideas.author_response: Palle does not need the RAND-number comparison; the unresolved problem is capturing the abacus blur, interesting in itself.

ideas.title: The blur is something the record keeps
ideas.idea: Losing the separability of individual marks can make repeated passage visible as density. A print treatment can either preserve or discard that phenomenon.
ideas.evidence: Raw Godot image already contains soft overlapping marks; contour conversion turns them into rings. A one-pixel continuous-tone conversion retains the gradients. Identical raw state and legacy contour output verified by native capture.
ideas.risk: Calling the result Gaussian without measuring it, conflating target distribution with an image filter, or inventing blur absent from the source.
ideas.next_test: For a later return: compare raw and tonal views at page size and ask what density reveals. No test is pending now; keep contour in the current chapter.
ideas.author_response: Keep the contour print now; return to this later (16 October 2026).
